Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates bilateral pulmonary nodules and prominent hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy, which corresponds to the CT findings in Figure 1a showing conglomerate nodal masses and peripheral nodules. This combination of bilateral hilar adenopathy with parenchymal nodules is characteristic of sarcoidosis (often referred to as the galaxy sign on CT when nodules coalesce), making it the most accurate description among the choices.
